date_note: GAME's customer email says the incident was detected during the week of 9 November; Roams says the email went out on 18 November. 19 November, the day of the first reports read, is the date used.
title: GAME says unauthorized access may have exposed customer contact details and order history
summary: Spanish video game retailer GAME emailed customers that unauthorized access to its systems, detected during the week of 9 November, may have compromised customer numbers, phone numbers, email addresses and order history. It says account passwords were not compromised and it does not store payment data. GAME has not said how many people are affected; Roams says it has not addressed earlier user reports of vanished account balances.
plain: Spanish game retailer GAME says someone got into its systems and may have seen customers' contact details and order history. It says passwords were not affected and it does not keep payment data.
exec: A national game retailer's customer contact data and order history may be exposed, which suits targeted phishing of its customers.
action: GAME's email advises customers to change their password and not reuse it elsewhere, and says GAME will never ask for passwords, personal data or validation codes.

validation.note: Follow-up 22 Nov: Geeknetic reproduces GAME's customer email in full and Roams reports it independently (both 19 Nov); Escudo Digital also relays it. GAME's email gives detection as the week of 9 November, not 9 November; corrected. No count, regulator notice or claimant in any page read.
